extracted.intended_audience: WUWM editorial staff and journalists (public radio employees)
extracted.subtask_description: A station-specific code of ethics and practices for WUWM journalists, describing standards for editorial independence, accuracy, fairness, conflicts of interest, fundraising/firewall rules, social media, outside activities, and disciplinary procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contribute to communities' civic, educational, and cultural life
rubrics_metrics.description: Public media organizations contribute to a strong civil society and active community life, provide access to knowledge and culture, extend education, and offer varied viewpoints and sensibilities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Present a range of ideas and cultures and offer a robust forum for discussion and debate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commit to accuracy and integrity
rubrics_metrics.description: Commit to accuracy and integrity in the pursuit of facts about events, issues, and important matters that affect communities and people’s lives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Diligent verification is critical; ensure statements of fact are correct and in context; place highest value on information gathered and verified by the organization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pursue fairness and responsiveness
rubrics_metrics.description: Pursue fairness and responsiveness in content and services, with particular attention to reflecting diversity of demography, culture, and beliefs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Gather responses from those who are subjects of criticism or unfavorable allegations; consider the strongest arguments on all sides and aim for nuance over appearance of balance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Aim for transparency in news gathering and editorial choices
rubrics_metrics.description: Aim for transparency in news gathering, reporting, and other content creation and share the reasons for important editorial and programming choices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain editorial decisions and be open about reporting methods and limitations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protect the editorial process from undue influence
rubrics_metrics.description: Protect the editorial process from the fact and appearance of undue influence, exercising care in seeking and accepting funds and setting careful boundaries between contributors and content creators.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid both reality and appearance of inappropriate influence when accepting contributions and grants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Encourage understanding of fundraising operations and disclosure of sponsor support
rubrics_metrics.description: Encourage understanding of fundraising operations and practices, acknowledge program sponsors, and disclose content-related terms of sponsor support.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be transparent about sponsorship terms and how funding relates (or does not relate) to coverage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain respectful and accountable relationships with contributors
rubrics_metrics.description: Maintain respectful and accountable relationships with individual and organizational contributors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Manage contributor interactions so they do not compromise editorial independence or the perception thereof.

rubrics_metrics.name: Seek editorial partnerships and apply standards to collaborations
rubrics_metrics.description: Seek editorial partnerships and collaborations to enhance capacity, perspective, timeliness, and relevance and apply public media standards to these arrangements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply the same integrity and editorial standards to partner-produced content and collaborations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Employees must uphold public media integrity on- and off-duty
rubrics_metrics.description: Expect employees to uphold public media’s integrity in their personal as well as their professional lives, understanding that employee actions, even when 'off the clock,' affect trust, integrity, credibility, and impartiality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize that private actions visible to the public can affect perceived impartiality and trust.

rubrics_metrics.name: Promote public interest in governance and leadership
rubrics_metrics.description: Promote the common good, the public interest, and these commitments to integrity and trustworthiness in organizational governance, leadership, and management.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Leaders should model and institutionalize the standards of integrity throughout organizational decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accuracy (journalistic principle)
rubrics_metrics.description: Our purpose is to pursue the truth. Diligent verification is critical. We take great care to ensure that statements of fact in our journalism are both correct and in context.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rigorously challenge claims encountered and the assumptions journalists bring; devote resources to present the fullest version of the truth; value information gathered and verified by staff.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fairness (journalistic principle)
rubrics_metrics.description: Treat those we interview and report on with scrupulous fairness, guided by a spirit of professionalism.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Gather responses from subjects of criticism; when quoting or editing, aim to be faithful to meaning; strive to consider strongest arguments on all sides; goal is to seek truth, not produce the appearance of balance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Completeness (journalistic principle)
rubrics_metrics.description: Do our best to report thoroughly and tell stories comprehensively; avoid errors of omission and partial truths.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include diverse voices and divergent views; if unable to deliver all answers, explain what is not yet known and work to fill gaps.

rubrics_metrics.name: Honesty (journalistic principle)
rubrics_metrics.description: Journalists conduct themselves honestly, attribute information received from others, avoid hyperbole and sensational conjecture, and do not mix fiction with news reporting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reveal any fabrication used as a hypothetical; identify oneself as a WUWM journalist when reporting; present information honestly without deception.

rubrics_metrics.name: Independence (journalistic principle)
rubrics_metrics.description: Primary allegiance is to the public. Any personal or professional interests that conflict with that allegiance, whether in appearance or reality, risk compromising credibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid conflicts of interest and appearances that could undermine the public’s trust.

rubrics_metrics.name: Impartiality (journalistic principle)
rubrics_metrics.description: Strive to report and produce stories that treat all views fairly and aggressively challenge our own perspectives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pursue a diverse range of viewpoints and aim to present the truth as completely as possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accountability (journalistic principle)
rubrics_metrics.description: Take full responsibility for our work and be ready and willing to answer for it, welcoming questions or criticisms from stakeholders.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Respond to the public; correct mistakes forthrightly, reflect on them, and learn from them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Respect (journalistic principle)
rubrics_metrics.description: Treat everyone affected by our journalism with decency and compassion; be civil and avoid arrogance; minimize undue harm.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be sensitive to cultural differences and privacy; take special care with those who are vulnerable or suffering; ask tough questions to seek answers, not confrontation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Excellence (journalistic principle)
rubrics_metrics.description: Marry important truths with engaging narrative and take pride in craftsmanship of storytelling, words, sounds and images.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Edit to add impact and clarity—not to slant or distort; avoid sensationalism and shallow sentimentality; faithfully and powerfully convey the truth.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclosure and recusal for divided loyalties
rubrics_metrics.description: Vigilantly disclose to supervisors any circumstances where loyalties may be divided — extending to interests of spouses and family members — and when necessary recuse from related coverage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recuse from coverage that creates a conflict; disclose family or spouse interests that could affect reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Political activity restrictions
rubrics_metrics.description: WUWM employees may not engage in political activity at work unless directly related to job duties; as journalists, they do not participate in political parties, campaigns, or causes (including contributions) and do not run for public office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not wear political or advocacy buttons at work; avoid political cartoons, stickers, or posters at workstations; do not sign petitions, write letters to the editor, speak at public meetings, or post yard signs relating to political or social issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Social media conduct
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognize that social networking blurs personal and professional lines; refrain from the same kind of political activity on social media as prohibited elsewhere.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Private communications on personal email to friends and family are excluded as not accessible to the public; avoid public social media political activity that compromises impartiality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restrictions on outside activities and freelance work
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not do outside work that is in direct competition with WUWM; outside freelance work that does not compete requires written permission from a supervisor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No public relations work (paid or unpaid); exceptions may be made for volunteer nonprofit, nonpartisan activities if not in conflict with WUWM reporting; consult supervisors when in doubt.

rubrics_metrics.name: Approval required for speaking engagements and media appearances
rubrics_metrics.description: Supervisors will approve speaking engagements with organizations that might have a relationship to a subject WUWM may cover; permission required for TV or other media appearances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: During outside appearances, do not express views that would not air in role as WUWM journalist.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plagiarism prohibition
rubrics_metrics.description: Plagiarism is an unforgivable offense. WUWM journalists do not take other people's work and present it as our own.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Always attribute sources and produce original work or properly attributed quotations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Diverse, unrestricted funding reinforces independence
rubrics_metrics.description: A large and diverse group of funders supports our work; most funding supports overall operations rather than specific programs. A diversity of sources, number of contributors, and unrestricted nature of funds reinforce editorial independence and integrity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritize unrestricted and diverse funding sources to reduce risk of influence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Careful attention to earmarked contributions and grants
rubrics_metrics.description: Give careful attention to contributions and grants that support specific programs, projects, and activities; seek to avoid the reality and appearance of inappropriate influence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate grants for potential conflicts; set boundaries between funders and editorial staff.

rubrics_metrics.name: Right to refuse donations
rubrics_metrics.description: Reserve the right to refuse any donation for any reason, including perceived conflicts of interest, potential audience misconception regarding a funder’s role or influence, and perceived impact on reputation, integrity, or fundraising ability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When in doubt, refuse or seek higher-level guidance to protect reputation and independence.

rubrics_metrics.name: No funding from political parties or candidates for ongoing news programming
rubrics_metrics.description: We do not accept funding of ongoing news and information programming from political parties and candidates for public office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Politically-affiliated funding is categorically excluded from supporting ongoing news programming.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not accept funding that obligates coverage
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not accept funding that would obligate us to provide coverage of a topic that we would not have covered with general funds or that requires more extensive coverage than the topic’s value or importance warrants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reject offers that create editorial obligations or distort the scope/extent of coverage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid discussing coverage planning with grant-making officials
rubrics_metrics.description: As a rule, we don’t discuss any coverage planning with grant-making officials.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain separation between grant-makers and editorial planning to prevent undue influence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Designated funder contacts
rubrics_metrics.description: The General Manager will designate individuals who will serve as contacts with funders for grant-making purposes or other communications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Channel funder communications through designated non-editorial contacts to protect editorial independence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Common-sense escalation and review process
rubrics_metrics.description: When an issue arises employees should discuss the matter with their supervisor; the supervisor should seek guidance from the General Manager; the GM may seek guidance of others with expertise in journalist ethics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow chain-of-command consultation; when necessary, the General Manager's decision is eligible for review by the Dean of the College of Letters and Science.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consequences for noncompliance
rubrics_metrics.description: WUWM employees who do not comply with the Code may be subject to disciplinary action up to and including termination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Noncompliance triggers standard disciplinary procedures; consult UW System Code of Ethics for additional requirements.
